{"conversation_history":[],"user_request":"Please mark all the oral continuation phenomena in the following paragraphs：Parachutes are big,heavy and bulky.Typical parachutes wouldn't fit beneath your plane seat.They would take up a lot of real estate on the plane and add to its overall weight.To tackle that,parachutes would be have to be made significantly smaller.Plus there would have to be systems in place to ensure that the parachute opens only when the passenger is ready to deploy it,and that they work seamlessly every time.All of these factors add to the overall cost of a single flight which needless to say the passengers would have to bear.As a result,ticket prices would soar and that's just bad news for the airline businesses.As such,money becomes a major deterrent for having parachutes on     board airplanes.It's important to realize that when the engines of a plane fail mid flight,the plane doesn't just drop out of the sky like a stone,it still has the ability to glide.Something that pilots use to execute an emergency landing when something goes wrong.\nAll in all,it's safe to say that if something goes wrong during a flight,passengers are safer if they remain strapped to their seats while the pilots attempt an emergency landing rather than jumping out of the plane at 40,000 feet.","candidate_answer":"## The passage with oral-continuation markers marked\n\nParachutes are big, heavy **and** bulky. Typical parachutes wouldn't fit beneath your plane seat. They would take up a lot of real estate on the plane **and** add to its overall weight. **To tackle that,** parachutes would be have to be made significantly smaller. **Plus** there would have to be systems in place to ensure that the parachute opens only when the passenger is ready to deploy it, **and that** they work seamlessly every time. **All of these factors** add to the overall cost of a single flight **which needless to say** the passengers would have to bear. **As a result,** ticket prices would soar **and that's just bad news** for the airline businesses. **As such,** money becomes a major deterrent for having parachutes on board airplanes. **It's important to realize that** when the engines of a plane fail mid flight, the plane doesn't just drop out of the sky like a stone, **it still has the ability to glide.** **Something that** pilots use to execute an emergency landing when something goes wrong.\n\n**All in all,** **it's safe to say that** if something goes wrong during a flight, passengers are safer if they remain strapped to their seats while the pilots attempt an emergency landing **rather than** jumping out of the plane at 40,000 feet.\n\n## Inventory of the marked items\n\n| # | Marker | Type | What it does in oral continuation |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| 1 | and (…big, heavy **and** bulky) | Additive coordinator | Chains one more item onto the list without re-planning the clause |\n| 2 | and (…take up a lot of real estate **and** add…) | Additive coordinator | Parataxis: adds a second predicate instead of a subordinate clause |\n| 3 | **To tackle that,** | Purpose / anaphoric frame | Sentence-initial link pointing back to the previous problem, keeping the argument moving |\n| 4 | **Plus** | Additive discourse marker | Typical spoken \"and also\" opener, stacking a further point |\n| 5 | **and that** (…ready to deploy it, **and that** they work…) | Additive / parallel complement | Continues the \"ensure that…\" complement with a second \"that\"-clause |\n| 6 | **All of these factors** | Summarising anaphor | Gathers up the preceding points and carries them forward as a subject |\n| 7 | **which needless to say** | Comment (parenthetical) relative | Stance aside spliced into the flow — evaluates while continuing |\n| 8 | **As a result,** | Resultative marker | Sentence-initial consequence link, the commonest spoken continuation signal |\n| 9 | **and that's just bad news** | Additive + evaluative comment | Tag-on clause that comments on the preceding statement |\n| 10 | **As such,** | Inferential marker | Draws the next conclusion from what has just been said |\n| 11 | **It's important to realize that** | Attention-directing frame | Metadiscursive opener that launches a new, emphasised point |\n| 12 | …, **it still has the ability to glide.** | Paratactic continuation (comma splice) | Loosely coordinated clause added in speech rhythm rather than subordination |\n| 13 | **Something that** … | Elaborative tail / appositive fragment | Separate \"sentence\" that continues and expands the previous noun phrase |\n| 14 | **All in all,** | Summative marker | Signals the wrap-up sequence |\n| 15 | **it's safe to say that** | Hedging / stance frame | Softens and introduces the concluding claim |\n| 16 | **rather than** | Contrastive linker | Sets up the final either/or contrast that closes the argument |\n\n## Notes on the pattern\n\n- **Sentence-initial linking adverbials** (*To tackle that, Plus, As a result, As such, All in all*) do most of the continuation work — they are the spoken equivalent of paragraph signposts.\n- **Additive chaining** (*and… and… and that*) reflects online planning: ideas are strung together rather than embedded.\n- **Comment/stance inserts** (*which needless to say, that's just bad news, it's safe to say that, it's important to realize that*) interrupt the syntax to keep the listener oriented.\n- **Loose right-hand extensions** (*it still has the ability to glide. Something that…*) are typically oral: the speaker adds after the fact what could have been a relative clause.\n\n(Original wording, including \"would be have to be\", has been kept unchanged; only the markers have been highlighted.)","checklist":[{"checklist_id":1,"criterion":"Does the response correctly identify all instances of oral continuation phenomena in the provided paragraphs?"},{"checklist_id":2,"criterion":"Are the identified oral continuation phenomena accurately labeled and described?"},{"checklist_id":3,"criterion":"Is the response free from factual and grammatical errors?"},{"checklist_id":4,"criterion":"Does the response address the specific task of marking oral continuation phenomena without deviating into unrelated content?"},{"checklist_id":5,"criterion":"Is the response clear and easy to understand, with appropriate use of terminology related to oral continuation phenomena?"},{"checklist_id":6,"criterion":"Does the response follow the formatting and structural guidelines implied by the query?"},{"checklist_id":7,"criterion":"Are all relevant oral continuation phenomena included, ensuring completeness of the response?"},{"checklist_id":8,"criterion":"Is the explanation, if provided, logical and does it enhance the understanding of the identified phenomena?"},{"checklist_id":9,"criterion":"Does the response maintain coherence and flow throughout the assessment of the paragraphs?"},{"checklist_id":10,"criterion":"Is the overall length of the response appropriate, neither too brief to be incomplete nor unnecessarily verbose?"}]}
